title.zh: 卷七十九下 儒林列傳
title.raw: 卷七十九下 儒林列傳 Volume 79b: Biographies of Confucian Scholars 2

sentences.zh: 《前書》魯人申公受《詩》於浮丘伯，為作詁訓，是為《魯詩》；

translations.literal: The Former Documents: Shen Gong of Lu received the Odes from Fuqiu Bo, for them made gloss and exegesis, and this is the 'Odes in the Lu tradition';
translations.idiomatic: The Han shu records that Shen Gong of Lu studied the Odes under Fuqiu Bo and compiled glosses—what became the Lu school of the classic.

sentences.zh: 齊人轅固生亦傳《詩》，是為《齊詩》；

translations.literal: Yuan Gu of Qi likewise transmitted the Odes, and this is the 'Odes in the Qi tradition';
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Gu of Qi handed down another line—the Qi Odes.

sentences.zh: 燕人韓嬰亦傳《詩》，是為《韓詩》；

translations.literal: Han Ying of Yan likewise transmitted the Odes, and this is the 'Odes in the Han tradition';
translations.idiomatic: Han Ying of Yan founded the Han school of the Odes.

sentences.zh: 三家皆立博士。

translations.literal: All three houses had Erudites established.
translations.idiomatic: All three received chairs at the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 趙人毛萇傳《詩》，是為《毛詩》，未得立。

translations.literal: Mao Chang of Zhao transmitted the Odes, and this is the 'Mao Odes'; it did not obtain establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Chang of Zhao taught what became the Mao commentary, which had no doctoral chair in Western Han.

sentences.zh: 1 高詡

translations.literal: 1 Gao Xu
translations.idiomatic: 1. Gao Xu

sentences.zh: 高詡字季回，平原般人也。

translations.literal: Gao Xu, courtesy name Jihui, was a man of Pan in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu, Jihui, came from Pan in Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖父嘉，以《魯詩》授元帝，仕至上谷太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jia, by the Lu Odes instructed Emperor Yuan, and in office reached Administrator of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jia had taught the Lu Odes to Emperor Yuan and risen to governor of Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 父容，少傳嘉學，哀、平間為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Rong, in youth transmitted Jia's learning, and between Emperors Ai and Ping became Grand Master of Splendid Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rong inherited Jia's scholarship and served as grand master of splendid carriages under Emperors Ai and Ping.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，除郎中。

translations.literal: He was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and appointed Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: A Filial-and-Incorrupt nomination brought him a gentleman's appointment.

sentences.zh: 建武中，入授皇太子《論語》，又為其章句。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu period he entered and instructed the heir apparent in the Analects, and also for him made chapter-and-verse glosses.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwu years he tutored the crown prince in the Analects and wrote a chapter-and-verse commentary for him.

sentences.zh: 拜諫議大夫、侍中、右中郎將。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grandee Remonstrant and Consultant, Palace Attendant, and Leader of Court Gentlemen of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grandee remonstrant, palace attendant, and leader of court gentlemen of the right.

sentences.zh: 永平五年，遷大鴻臚。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongping he was promoted to Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: In 62 CE he became grand herald.

sentences.zh: 每進見，錫以几杖，入屏不趨，贊事不名。

translations.literal: Whenever he advanced to audience, he was granted a stool and staff; entering the screen he did not hasten his step; in announcing affairs he was not named.
translations.idiomatic: At each audience the emperor gave him a seat and staff, waived the rule that he must hurry past the screen, and had him announced without his personal name.

sentences.zh: 經傳有疑，輒遣小黃門就舍即問。

translations.literal: When there were doubts in the classics and commentaries, he always dispatched a junior Yellow Gate to his residence to question him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the throne puzzled over a classical passage, a junior eunuch would be sent to Xu's house for an immediate ruling.

sentences.zh: 顯宗以咸有師傅恩，而素清苦，常特賞賜珍玩束帛，奉祿增於諸卿，咸皆散與諸生之貧者。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong, because Gao Xu had the grace of a tutor to the heir and was by nature pure and austere, constantly specially bestowed rare treasures and bundled silks, increased his salary above the various ministers, and Gao Xu always scattered it all to poor students.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming honored Gao Xu as a former tutor of the crown prince: knowing his frugal habits, he showered him with gifts and a stipend above the usual ministerial rate, and Xu passed every cash string to needy students.

sentences.zh: 病篤、帝親輦駕臨視。

translations.literal: When his illness was grave, the emperor personally with the palanquin carriage came to look in on him.
translations.idiomatic: When he lay dying, the emperor drove his own carriage to his bedside.

sentences.zh: 八年，年七十二，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, at age seventy-two, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in 65 CE at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 子福，拜郎中，亦以《論語》入授和帝。

translations.literal: His son Fu was appointed Gentleman of the Palace and likewise by the Analects entered to instruct Emperor He.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gao Fu became a gentleman of the palace and likewise tutored Emperor He in the Analects.

sentences.zh: 魏應字君伯，任城人也。

translations.literal: Wei Ying, courtesy name Junbo, was a man of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ying, Junbo, was a native of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 少好學。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books from boyhood.

sentences.zh: 建武初，詣博士受業，習《魯詩》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he went to an Erudite to receive instruction and studied the Lu Odes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwu era he enrolled under an Erudite and mastered the Lu Odes.

sentences.zh: 閉門誦習，不交僚黨，京師稱之。

translations.literal: He closed his gate to recite and practice, did not associate with official cliques, and the capital praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He shut himself in to memorize the text, shunned political cliques, and won praise in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後歸為郡吏，舉明經，除濟陰王文學。

translations.literal: Later he returned and became a commandery clerk; he was recommended as Understanding the Classics and appointed erudite of letters to the king of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: He went home as a commandery clerk, took a classical-learning nomination, and became tutor to the king of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 以疾免官，教授山澤中，徒眾常數百人。

translations.literal: On account of illness he was dismissed from office; he taught in mountains and marshes, and his followers were constantly several hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Ill health ended his post; he taught in the hill country and seldom addressed fewer than a few hundred pupils.

sentences.zh: 永平初，為博士，再遷侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongping he became an Erudite, and after two promotions became Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongping era he took an Erudite chair, then rose twice to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷大鴻臚。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: In 70 CE he became grand herald.

sentences.zh: 十八年，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: In 75 CE he was named grand master of splendid carriages.

sentences.zh: 建初四年，拜五官中郎將，詔入授千乘王伉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianchu he was appointed General of the Household for All Purposes and was ordered by edict to enter and instruct the king of Qiancheng, Kang.
translations.idiomatic: In 79 CE he became a general of the household and was ordered to tutor Prince Kang of Qiancheng.

sentences.zh: 應經明行修，弟子自遠方至，著錄數千人。

translations.literal: Ying's classics were clear and his conduct cultivated; disciples came from distant places, and those recorded on the rolls were several thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned for learning and character, he drew thousands of students from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 肅宗甚重之，數進見，論難於前，特受賞賜。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong greatly esteemed him, repeatedly advanced him to audience, debated difficult points before him, and he specially received rewards and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang held him in high regard, often summoned him for disputations on the dais, and heaped gifts on him.

sentences.zh: 時會京師諸儒於白虎觀，講論《五經》同異，使應專掌難問，侍中淳于恭奏之，帝親臨稱制，如石渠故事。

translations.literal: At that time the court convened the various Confucians of the capital at the White Tiger Hall, lectured and discussed sameness and difference in the Five Classics, ordered Ying solely to preside over difficult questioning, Palace Attendant Chunyu Gong memorialized it, and the emperor personally attended and pronounced decisions, according to the precedent of Stone Canal.
translations.idiomatic: When the court gathered classicists at the White Tiger Hall to debate the Five Classics, Wei Ying was put in charge of the floor; Chunyu Gong reported the proceedings, and the emperor presided in person after the manner of the Western Han debates at Stone Canal.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為上黨太守，徵拜騎都尉，卒於官。

translations.literal: The next year he went out to become Administrator of Shangdang; he was summoned and appointed Chief Commandant of Cavalry, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became governor of Shangdang, was recalled as chief commandant of cavalry, and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 伏恭字叔齊，琅邪東武人，司徒湛之兄子也。

translations.literal: Fu Gong, courtesy name Shuqi, was a man of Dongwu in Langye, a nephew by the elder brother of Minister of Education Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gong, Shuqi, of Dongwu in Langye, was a nephew of Minister of Education Fu Zhan.

sentences.zh: 湛弟黯，字稚文，以明《齊詩》，改定章句，作《解說》九篇，位至光祿勳，無子，以恭為後。

translations.literal: Zhan's younger brother An, courtesy name Zhiwen, because he was clear in the Qi Odes, revised and fixed chapter-and-verse glosses, composed nine chapters of 'Explanatory Discourse,' reached office as Superintendent of the Imperial Household, had no son, and took Gong as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhan's brother Fu An, Zhiwen, was an authority on the Qi Odes who rewrote the chapter glosses and published nine essays on the text; he rose to superintendent of the imperial household and, childless, adopted Fu Gong as his heir.

sentences.zh: 恭性孝，事所繼母甚謹，少傳黯學，以任為郎。

translations.literal: Gong by nature was filial; in serving the stepmother whom he had inherited he was very careful; in youth he transmitted An's learning, and by privilege appointment became a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial toward his adoptive mother, he mastered Fu An's scholarship in youth and entered the court on a privilege appointment.

sentences.zh: 建武四年，除劇令。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu he was appointed magistrate of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In 28 CE he was named magistrate of the difficult county of Ji.

sentences.zh: 視事十三年，以惠政公廉聞。

translations.literal: Holding office thirteen years, he was heard of for benevolent governance and fair incorruptness.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen years in office earned him a reputation for humane and incorrupt rule.

sentences.zh: 青州舉為尤異，太常試經第一，拜博士，遷常山太守。

translations.literal: Qing province recommended him as outstandingly unusual; the Grand Chamberlain examined him on the classics in first place; he was appointed Erudite and promoted to Administrator of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou nominated him as an outstanding official; he topped the Grand Chamberlain's classical examination, took an Erudite chair, and became governor of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 郭修學校，教授不輟，由是北州多為伏氏學。

translations.literal: He enlarged and cultivated schools, and teaching did not cease; whereby in the northern province many practiced the Fu house learning.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded the county schools and never stopped lecturing until the northern provinces swarmed with students of the Fu line.

sentences.zh: 永平二年，代梁松為太僕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongping he replaced Liang Song as Grand Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: In 59 CE he succeeded Liang Song as grand coachman.

sentences.zh: 四年，帝臨辟雍，於行禮中拜恭為司空，儒者以為榮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the emperor attended the Circular Moat; in the midst of performing the rites he appointed Gong Minister of Works, and Confucians deemed it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: In 61 CE, during the suburban rites at the Circular Moat, the emperor named him minister of work—a moment classicists still cite with pride.

sentences.zh: 初，父黯章句繁多，恭乃省減浮辭，定為二十萬言。

translations.literal: At first, his father An's chapter-and-verse glosses were numerous; Gong thereupon reduced and cut floating phrases, fixing them at two hundred thousand graphs.
translations.idiomatic: His adoptive father Fu An's gloss had grown unwieldy; Fu Gong pruned the verbiage down to two hundred thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 在位九年，以病乞骸骨罷，詔賜千石奉以終其身。

translations.literal: Holding office nine years, on account of illness he begged for his bones and was dismissed; an edict granted him a salary of one thousand piculs to end his life.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years he retired ill; the court granted him a full thousand-picul stipend for life.

sentences.zh: 十五年，行幸琅邪，引遇如三公儀。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, on a progress to Langye, he was drawn forward and received with the ceremony due the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In 72 CE, when the emperor toured Langye, Fu Gong was received with the honors due a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 建初二年冬，肅宗行饗禮，以恭為三老。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Jianchu, Suzong performed the communal banquet rite and took Gong as one of the Three Elders.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 77 CE Emperor Zhang held the state banquet and named Fu Gong one of the Three Elders.

sentences.zh: 年九十，元和元年卒，賜葬顯節陵下。

translations.literal: At age ninety, in the first year of Yuanhe he died, and burial was granted below Xianjie Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 84 CE at ninety and was buried beside Emperor Ming's tomb with imperial honors.

sentences.zh: 子壽，官至東郡太守。

translations.literal: His son Shou reached office as Administrator of the eastern commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu Shou rose to governor of the eastern commandery.

sentences.zh: 任末字叔本，蜀郡繁人也。

translations.literal: Ren Mo, courtesy name Shuben, was a man of Fan in Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Mo, Shuben, came from Fan in Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 少習《齊詩》，遊京師，教授十餘年。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Qi Odes, roamed the capital, and taught more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He trained in the Qi Odes, studied in Luoyang, and taught there for over a decade.

sentences.zh: 友人董奉德於洛陽病亡，末乃躬推鹿車，載奉德喪致其墓所，由是知名。

translations.literal: His friend Dong Fengde died of illness in Luoyang; Mo thereupon personally pushed a deer cart, loaded Fengde's bier, and delivered it to his grave site, whereby he became known.
translations.idiomatic: When his friend Dong Fengde died in Luoyang, Ren Mo hauled the coffin on a handcart to the burial ground himself and won fame for it.

sentences.zh: 為郡功曹，辭以病免。

translations.literal: He became merit assessor for the commandery, but declined citing illness and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly served as merit assessor, then resigned on grounds of health.

sentences.zh: 後奔師喪，於道物故。

translations.literal: Later he ran to a teacher's funeral and on the road passed away.
translations.idiomatic: He later set out to mourn a teacher and died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 臨命，敕兄子造曰：「必致我屍於師門，使死而有知，魂靈不慚；

translations.literal: Facing death, he instructed his elder brother's son Zao, saying: 'You must bring my corpse to my teacher's gate, so that if after death there is knowledge, my soul will not be ashamed;
translations.idiomatic: Near death he told his nephew Zao, "Lay my body at my teacher's door—if the dead know, my spirit need not hang its head;

sentences.zh: 如其無知，得土而已。

translations.literal: if there is no knowledge, obtaining earth is enough.'
translations.idiomatic: if not, any soil will do."

sentences.zh: 」造從之。

translations.literal: ' Zao followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Zao did as he asked.

sentences.zh: 景鸞字漢伯，廣漢梓潼人也。

translations.literal: Jing Luan, courtesy name Hanbo, was a man of Zitong in Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Luan, Hanbo, was from Zitong in Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 少隨師學經，涉七州之地。

translations.literal: In youth he followed teachers studying the classics, traversing the territory of seven provinces.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he studied under many masters and traveled through seven provinces.

sentences.zh: 能理《齊詩》、《施氏易》、兼受《河》、《洛》圖緯，作《易說》及《詩解》，文​​句兼取《河》、《洛》，以類相從，名為《交集》。

translations.literal: He was able to order the Qi Odes and the Changes in the Shi tradition; concurrently he received River and Luo chart-prophecies; he composed 'Discourse on the Changes' and 'Explication of the Odes,' and in phrases concurrently took River and Luo, grouping by category, naming it 'Interwoven Collection.'
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Qi Odes and the Shi Changes, absorbed the River and Luo apocrypha, and wrote treatises on the Changes and Odes that wove canonical text with prophetic lore in a work he called the Interwoven Collection.

sentences.zh: 又撰《禮內外記》，號曰《禮略》。

translations.literal: Further he compiled 'Inner and Outer Records on the Rites,' styled 'Rites in Brief.'
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled inner and outer notes on the Rites under the title Rites in Brief.

sentences.zh: 又抄風角雜書，列其占驗，作《興道》一篇。

translations.literal: Further he excerpted miscellaneous books on wind-horns, arrayed their divinatory verifications, and composed one chapter 'Raising the Way.'
translations.idiomatic: He abstracted works on wind-omen divination, listed their predictive hits, and wrote a chapter called Raising the Way.

sentences.zh: 及作《月令章句》。

translations.literal: And he composed 'Chapter-and-Verse Glosses on the Monthly Ordinances.'
translations.idiomatic: He produced a chapter-and-verse gloss on the Monthly Ordinances as well.

sentences.zh: 凡所著述五十餘萬言。

translations.literal: In all, what he wrote and composed was more than five hundred thousand graphs.
translations.idiomatic: His published corpus exceeded half a million characters.

sentences.zh: 數上書陳救災變之術。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he submitted memorials setting forth techniques for saving calamitous portents.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized on how to avert disaster and prodigies.

sentences.zh: 州郡辟命不就，以壽終。

translations.literal: Provincial and commandery summons orders he did not accept; he ended by a full lifespan.
translations.idiomatic: He turned down every provincial and commandery appointment and died at home in old age.

sentences.zh: 薛漢字公子，淮陽人也。

translations.literal: Xue Han, courtesy name Gongzi, was a man of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Han, Gongzi, was a native of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 世習《韓詩》，父子以章句著名。

translations.literal: For generations the family practiced the Han Odes; father and son were famous for chapter-and-verse glosses.
translations.idiomatic: The family had taught the Han Odes for generations; father and son were famed for their glosses.

sentences.zh: 漢少傳父業，尤善說災異讖緯，教授常數百人。

translations.literal: Han in youth transmitted the father's enterprise, was especially good at expounding calamitous portents and chart-prophecies, and in teaching constantly had several hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Han inherited his father's school, excelled at correlating disasters with apocrypha, and kept several hundred students.

sentences.zh: 建武初，為博士，受詔校定圖讖。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he became an Erudite and received an edict to collate and fix chart-prophecies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangwu's reign he became an Erudite and was ordered to edit the prophetic corpus.

sentences.zh: 當世言《詩》者，推漢為長。

translations.literal: Among those of the age who spoke of the Odes, they pushed Han as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries ranked him first among Odes scholars.

sentences.zh: 永平中，為千乘太守，政有異跡。

translations.literal: In the Yongping period he became Administrator of Qiancheng; his governance had unusual traces.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongping era he governed Qiancheng with a record that drew notice at court.

sentences.zh: 後坐楚事辭相連，下獄死。

translations.literal: Later he sat in guilt because Chu-case words linked him; he was cast into prison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later implicated in the Chu conspiracy, jailed, and died there.

sentences.zh: 弟子犍為杜撫、會稽澹台敬伯、鉅鹿韓伯高最知名。

translations.literal: Among disciples, Du Fu of Qianwei, Tantai Jingbo of Kuaiji, and Han Bogao of Julu were most known by name.
translations.idiomatic: His best-known pupils were Du Fu of Qianwei, Tantai Jingbo of Kuaiji, and Han Bogao of Julu.

sentences.zh: 杜撫字叔和，犍為武陽人也。

translations.literal: Du Fu, courtesy name Shuhe, was a man of Wuyang in Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fu, Shuhe, came from Wuyang in Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 少有高才。

translations.literal: In youth he had lofty talent.
translations.idiomatic: He showed exceptional gifts early.

sentences.zh: 受業於薛漢，定《韓詩章句》。

translations.literal: He received instruction under Xue Han and fixed the chapter-and-verse glosses of the Han Odes.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Xue Han and produced a definitive chapter gloss on the Han Odes.

sentences.zh: 後歸鄉里教授。

translations.literal: Later he returned to his home village and taught.
translations.idiomatic: He then went home and opened a private school.

sentences.zh: 沈靜樂道，舉動必以禮。

translations.literal: He was deep, still, and delighted in the Way; in movement and rest he always used ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and devoted to the Way, he let ritual govern every action.

sentences.zh: 弟子千餘人。

translations.literal: Disciples were more than a thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: He taught more than a thousand students.

sentences.zh: 後為驃騎將軍東平王蒼所辟，及蒼就國，掾史悉補王官屬，未滿歲，皆自劾歸。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned by General of Agile Cavalry, the king of Dongping, Cang; when Cang went to his state, clerks and aides were all supplemented as royal household officials; before a full year had passed, they all impeached themselves and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Liu Cang of Dongping took him on staff; when the prince went to his fief, every aide was given a place in the princely household, but within a year they had all asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 時，撫為大夫，不忍去，蒼聞，賜車馬財物遣之。

translations.literal: At that time Fu was a grandee and could not bear to depart; Cang heard, bestowed chariot, horses, and goods, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fu, now a senior official, could not bear to leave; Liu Cang heard of it and sent him off with horses, a carriage, and gifts.

sentences.zh: 辟太尉府。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the Grand Commandant's office.
translations.idiomatic: The grand commandant's bureau then summoned him.

sentences.zh: 建初中，為公車令，數月卒官。

translations.literal: In the early Jianchu period he became overseer of the imperial coach; within several months he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhang he became overseer of the imperial coach and died in office a few months later.

sentences.zh: 其所作《詩題約義通》，學者傳之，曰《杜君法》云。

translations.literal: What he composed, 'Odes: Topics Binding Meaning Through,' scholars transmitted it, calling it 'Lord Du's Method,' it is said.
translations.idiomatic: His Odes: Topics Binding Meaning Through circulated among scholars as Master Du's method.

sentences.zh: 召馴字伯春，九江壽春人也。

translations.literal: Shao Xun, courtesy name Bochun, was a man of Shouchun in Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xun, Bochun, was from Shouchun in Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖信臣，元帝時為少府。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xinchen, in the time of Emperor Yuan, was Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shao Xinchen had been privy treasurer under Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 父建武中為卷令，俶儻不拘小節。

translations.literal: His father, in the Jianwu period, was magistrate of Juan, untrammeled and not bound by small points.
translations.idiomatic: His father had been magistrate of Juan under Guangwu—a man of bold spirit who scorned petty convention.

sentences.zh: 孫休，位至青州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandson Xiu reached office as Inspector of Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shao Xiu rose to provincial inspector of Qing.

sentences.zh: 楊仁字文義，巴郡閬中人也。

translations.literal: Yang Ren, courtesy name Wenyi, was a man of Langzhong in Ba commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ren, Wenyi, came from Langzhong in Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 建武中，詣師學習《韓詩》，數年歸，靜居教授。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu period he went to a teacher to study the Han Odes; after several years he returned and in quiet residence taught.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwu years he studied the Han Odes under a master, then came home and taught in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 仕郡為功曹，舉孝廉，除郎。

translations.literal: He served the commandery as merit assessor, was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, and was appointed gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He became commandery merit assessor, won a Filial-and-Incorrupt nomination, and received a gentleman's appointment.

sentences.zh: 太常上仁經中博士，仁自以年未五十，不應舊科，上府讓選。

translations.literal: The Grand Chamberlain submitted Ren as passing the Erudite examination on the classics; Ren himself considered that his years had not yet reached fifty and did not answer the old rule, and upward to the office declined selection.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Chamberlain nominated him for an Erudite chair, but Yang Ren, still under fifty, thought himself ineligible under the old rule and declined the nomination.

sentences.zh: 顯宗特詔補北宮衛士令，引見，問當世政跡。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong specially by edict appointed him overseer of guards for the Northern Palace, led him to audience, and asked about the age's administrative traces.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming specially named him captain of the Northern Palace guard, received him in audience, and asked his views on current government.

sentences.zh: 仁對以寬和任賢，抑黜驕戚為先。

translations.literal: Ren replied with lenience and harmony, employing the worthy, and suppressing and dismissing the arrogant among kin as first.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ren urged leniency, the appointment of worthy men, and checking the excesses of powerful consort clans as the first priorities.

sentences.zh: 又上便宜十二事，皆當世急務。

translations.literal: Further he submitted twelve opportune-convenience matters, all urgent tasks of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized twelve practical measures, each addressing an urgent problem of the day.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，賜以縑錢。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and granted him silk and cash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and rewarded him with silk and money.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，時諸馬貴盛，各爭欲入宮，仁被甲持戟，嚴勒門衛，莫敢輕進者。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, at that time the various Ma were noble and flourishing; each strove wishing to enter the palace; Ren donned armor and grasped a halberd, strictly commanded the gate guards, and none dared lightly to advance.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming's death the Ma clan tried to force the palace gates; Yang Ren armored himself, took a halberd, and held the guard line so firmly that no one dared rush the doors.

sentences.zh: 肅宗既立，諸馬共譖仁刻峻，帝知其忠，愈善之，拜什邡令。

translations.literal: After Suzong was established, the various Ma together slandered Ren as harsh and severe; the emperor knew his loyalty, was all the more good to him, and appointed him magistrate of Shifang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhang came to the throne the Ma faction slandered Yang Ren as harsh, but the emperor knew him for loyal, treated him with greater favor, and named him magistrate of Shifang.

sentences.zh: 寬惠為政，勸課掾史弟子，悉令就學。

translations.literal: With lenience and kindness he governed; he exhorted and set tasks for clerks' and aides' disciples, ordering all to go to study.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with kindness and ordered every clerk and clerk's son in the county to attend school.

sentences.zh: 其有通明經術者，顯之右署，或貢之朝，由是義學大興。

translations.literal: Those among them who penetrated and clarified classical arts, he displayed in the right offices, or presented them to the court; whereby righteous learning greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who mastered the classics was given a post on the right wing of the yamen or recommended to the capital, and learning flourished county-wide.

sentences.zh: 墾田千餘頃。

translations.literal: He opened more than a thousand qing of farmland for reclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Under his administration more than a thousand qing of new fields were brought under the plough.

sentences.zh: 行兄喪去官。

translations.literal: He left office to observe mourning for an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 後辟司徒桓虞府。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned to the bureau of Minister of Education Huan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recruited to the staff of Minister of Education Huan Yu.

sentences.zh: 掾有宋章者，貪奢不法，仁終不與交言同席，時人畏其節。

translations.literal: Among the clerks was one Song Zhang, greedy and extravagant and lawless; Ren to the end did not exchange words with him or share a mat, and people of the time stood in awe of his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk named Song Zhang was corrupt and flashy; Yang Ren refused ever to speak with him or sit beside him, and contemporaries respected his steel.

sentences.zh: 後為閬中令，卒於官。

translations.literal: Later he became magistrate of Langzhong and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as magistrate of Langzhong and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 趙曄字長君，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Ye, courtesy name Changjun, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ye, Changjun, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 少嘗為縣吏，奉檄迎督郵，曄恥於斯役，遂棄車馬去。

translations.literal: In youth he once was a county clerk; carrying a summons to welcome the touring inspector, Ye was ashamed of such service, threw away chariot and horses, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Once, as a county clerk ordered to greet the touring inspector, he found the errand beneath him, abandoned his carriage, and walked away.

sentences.zh: 到犍為資中，詣杜撫受《韓詩》，究竟其術。

translations.literal: He reached Zizhong in Qianwei and went to Du Fu to receive the Han Odes, exhausting their techniques.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Zizhong in Qianwei to study the Han Odes under Du Fu to the bottom of the tradition.

sentences.zh: 積二十年，絕問不還，家為發喪制服。

translations.literal: For twenty years he cut off correspondence and did not return; his family for him held a funeral and donned mourning.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years he sent no word home; his family assumed he was dead and went into mourning.

sentences.zh: 撫卒乃歸。

translations.literal: Only when Fu died did he return.
translations.idiomatic: He came home only after Du Fu died.

sentences.zh: 州召補從事，不就。

translations.literal: The province summoned him to fill a staff post; he did not take it up.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial government offered him a staff appointment; he declined.

sentences.zh: 舉有道。

translations.literal: He was recommended as Possessing the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He received a nomination as a man of moral attainment.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 曄著《吳越春秋》、《詩細歷神淵》。

translations.literal: Ye authored Spring and Autumn of Wu and Yue, and Odes in Fine Detail: Penetrating the Divine Abyss.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Spring and Autumn of Wu and Yue and a work on the Odes subtitled Penetrating the Divine Abyss.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕至會稽，讀《詩細》而歎息，以為長於《論衡》。

translations.literal: When Cai Yong reached Kuaiji and read Odes in Fine Detail he sighed, deeming it superior to Balanced Discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong, visiting Kuaiji, read the Odes treatise and declared it finer than Wang Chong's Balanced Discourse.

sentences.zh: 邕還京師，傳之，學者咸誦習焉。

translations.literal: When Yong returned to the capital he circulated it, and scholars all recited and practiced it.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Luoyang Cai Yong circulated the text until scholars everywhere were studying it.

sentences.zh: 時，山陽張匡，字文通，亦習《韓詩》，作章句。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Kuang of Shanyang, courtesy name Wentong, likewise studied the Han Odes and composed chapter-and-verse glosses.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time Zhang Kuang of Shanyang, Wentong, also taught the Han Odes and wrote glosses.

sentences.zh: 後舉有道，博士徵，不就。

translations.literal: Later he was recommended as Possessing the Way; an Erudite summons came, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated for moral stature and summoned as an Erudite, he refused both.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 衛宏字敬仲，東海人也。

translations.literal: Wei Hong, courtesy name Jingzhong, was a man of the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hong, Jingzhong, hailed from Donghai.

sentences.zh: 少與河南鄭興俱好古學。

translations.literal: In youth he and Zheng Xing of Henan together loved ancient learning.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and Zheng Xing of Henan shared a passion for archaic texts.

sentences.zh: 初，九江謝曼卿善《毛詩》，乃為其訓。

translations.literal: At first Xie Manqing of Jiujiang was good at the Mao Odes and for them made glosses.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Manqing of Jiujiang first mastered the Mao Odes and wrote a commentary.

sentences.zh: 宏從曼卿受學，因作《毛詩序》，善得《風雅》之旨，於今傳於世。

translations.literal: Hong received learning from Manqing, thereupon composed the Preface to the Mao Odes, skillfully grasping the intent of the Airs and Elegances, and to this day it circulates in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hong studied under Xie and composed the preface to the Mao Odes that still captures the spirit of the Airs and Elegances and remains standard today.

sentences.zh: 後從大司空杜林更受《古文尚書》，為作《訓旨》。

translations.literal: Later from Grand Minister of Works Du Lin he again received the Documents in ancient script, and for them composed Gloss on the Meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He later studied the archaic-text Documents under Grand Minister of Works Du Lin and wrote a gloss on their meaning.

sentences.zh: 時濟南徐巡師事宏，後從林受學，亦以儒顯，由是古學大興。

translations.literal: At that time Xu Xun of Jinan took Hong as teacher; later Xun received learning from Lin as well, and also became illustrious as a Confucian; whereby ancient-script learning greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xun of Jinan first studied under Wei Hong, then under Du Lin, and rose to classical fame himself, so that the archaic-text school flourished.

sentences.zh: 光武以為議郎。

translations.literal: Guangwu appointed him Gentleman Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu named him a gentleman consultant.

sentences.zh: 宏作《漢舊儀》四篇，以載西京雜事；

translations.literal: Hong composed four chapters of Han Old Protocols to record miscellaneous matters of Western capital Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: His four scrolls of Han Old Protocols preserve anecdotes of the Western capital;

sentences.zh: 又著賦、頌、誄七首，皆傳於世。

translations.literal: further he composed seven fu, eulogies, and dirges, all of which circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: he also left seven rhapsodies, eulogies, and dirges still read today.

sentences.zh: 中興後，鄭眾、賈逵傳《毛詩》，後馬融作《毛詩傳》，鄭玄作《毛詩箋》。

translations.literal: After the restoration Zheng Zhong and Jia Kui transmitted the Mao Odes, later Ma Rong composed Tradition on the Mao Odes, and Zheng Xuan composed Interlinear Notes on the Mao Odes.
translations.idiomatic: After the Han restoration Zheng Zhong and Jia Kui taught the Mao Odes; Ma Rong wrote a subcommentary and Zheng Xuan the famous interlinear notes.

sentences.zh: 《前書》魯高堂生，漢興傳《禮》十七篇。

translations.literal: The Former Documents: Gao Tang Sheng of Lu, when Han rose, transmitted the Rites in seventeen chapters.
translations.idiomatic: The Han shu records that Gao Tang Sheng of Lu taught the seventeen-chapter Rites when the dynasty was founded.

sentences.zh: 後瑕丘蕭奮以授同郡後蒼，蒼授梁人戴德及德兄子聖、沛人慶普。

translations.literal: Later Xiao Fen of Xiaqiu handed them on to Hou Cang of the same commandery, and Cang handed them on to Dai De of Liang and De's elder brother's son Sheng, and Qing Pu of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed from Xiao Fen of Xiaqiu to Hou Cang, then to Dai De of Liang, Dai De's nephew Dai Sheng, and Qing Pu of Pei.

sentences.zh: 於是德為《大戴禮》，聖為《小戴禮》，普為《慶氏禮》，三家皆立博士。

translations.literal: Thereupon De made the Elder Dai Rites, Sheng made the Younger Dai Rites, and Pu made the Qing Rites; all three houses had Erudites established.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Elder Dai, Younger Dai, and Qing recensions of the Rites, each with its own doctoral chair.

sentences.zh: 孔安國所獻《禮》古經五十六篇及《周官經》六篇，前世傳其書，未有名家。

translations.literal: The ancient-text Rites in fifty-six chapters that Kong Anguo presented, and the Offices of Zhou in six chapters, earlier generations transmitted these writings, but there was no specialist house.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo's fifty-six-chapter archaic Rites and the six scrolls of the Offices of Zhou circulated without a dominant scholarly school.

sentences.zh: 中興已後，亦有《大》、《小戴》博士，雖相傳不絕，然未有顯於儒林者。

translations.literal: After the restoration there were also Erudites for the Elder and Younger Dai Rites; although transmission did not cease, none became prominent in the Forest of Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han still appointed Dai Erudites, yet no master of those lines won a major place among court classicists.

sentences.zh: 建武中，曹充習慶氏學，傳其子褒，遂撰《漢禮》，事在《褒傳》。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu period Cao Chong studied the Qing house learning, transmitted it to his son Bao, and thereupon compiled Han Rites—the matter is in Bao's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangwu, Cao Chong studied the Qing tradition and passed it to his son Cao Bao, who codified Han court ritual as told in Cao Bao's biography.

sentences.zh: 董鈞字文伯，犍為資中人也。

translations.literal: Dong Jun, courtesy name Wenbo, was a man of Zizhong in Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jun, Wenbo, was from Zizhong in Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 習《慶氏禮》。

translations.literal: He studied the Qing Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He trained in the Qing recension of the Rites.

sentences.zh: 事大鴻臚王臨。

translations.literal: He served Grand Herald Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the staff of Grand Herald Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 元始中，舉明經，遷禀犧令。

translations.literal: In the Yuanshi period he was recommended as Understanding the Classics and promoted to overseer of the sacrificial granary (office title as in text: 禀犧令).
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Mang's Yuanshi era he took a classical nomination and became overseer of the imperial sacrifice granary.

sentences.zh: 病去官。

translations.literal: On account of illness he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to resign.

sentences.zh: 建武中，舉孝廉，辟司徒府。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu period he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and summoned to the Minister of Education's office.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu nominated him Filial and Incorrupt and called him to the minister of education's bureau.

sentences.zh: 鈞博通古今，數言政事。

translations.literal: Jun was broadly conversant with antiquity and the present, and repeatedly spoke on administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jun ranged widely over past and present and often spoke on policy.

sentences.zh: 永平初，為博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongping he became an Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongping era he took an Erudite chair.

sentences.zh: 時草創五郊祭祀，及宗廟禮樂，威儀章服，輒令鈞參議，多見從用，當世稱為通儒。

translations.literal: At that time the Five Suburban Sacrifices and ancestral-temple ritual music were being first established; in ritual bearing, insignia, and robes they always ordered Jun to join the deliberation; much was adopted from his views, and his age styled him a thoroughly learned Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: When the court first designed the five suburban sacrifices and temple music, regalia, and vestments, Dong Jun was always asked to advise; the throne adopted most of his counsel and hailed him as a universal scholar.

sentences.zh: 累遷五官中郎將，常教授門生百餘人。

translations.literal: He was cumulatively promoted to General of the Household for All Purposes and constantly taught more than a hundred disciples at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to general of the household for all purposes, he still kept more than a hundred students at his door.

sentences.zh: 後坐事左轉騎都尉。

translations.literal: Later on account of an affair he was shifted left to Chief Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: A later demotion made him chief commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘，卒於家。

translations.literal: At more than seventy years he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 中興，鄭眾傳《周官經》，後馬融作《周官傳》，授鄭玄，玄作《周官注》。

translations.literal: At the restoration Zheng Zhong transmitted the Offices of Zhou; later Ma Rong composed Tradition on the Offices of Zhou, handed it on to Zheng Xuan, and Xuan composed Commentary on the Offices of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhong taught the Offices of Zhou after the restoration; Ma Rong wrote a tradition, Ma's pupil Zheng Xuan a commentary, and the text became canonical.

sentences.zh: 玄本習《小戴禮》，後以古經校之，取其義長者，故為鄭氏學。

translations.literal: Xuan originally studied the Younger Dai Rites, later collated them with the ancient-text recension, taking whichever meaning was superior; hence there is the Zheng house learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan began with the Younger Dai Rites, compared them with the archaic scrolls, and kept the stronger reading at each point—hence the Zheng synthesis.

sentences.zh: 玄又注小戴所傳《禮記》四十九篇，通為《三禮》焉。

translations.literal: Xuan also annotated the forty-nine chapters of the Record of Rites transmitted by Younger Dai, completing in all the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He also glossed the forty-nine chapters of the Record of Rites in the Younger Dai line, completing his trilogy on the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 《前書》齊胡母子都傳《公羊春秋》，授東平贏公，贏公授東海孟卿，孟卿授魯人眭孟，眭孟授東海嚴彭祖、魯人顏安樂。

translations.literal: The Former Documents: Hu Muzi of Qi transmitted the Gongyang Spring and Autumn, handed it on to Ying Gong of Dongping, Ying Gong handed it on to Meng Qing of the Eastern Sea, Meng Qing handed it on to Sui Meng of Lu, and Sui Meng handed it on to Yan Pengzu of the Eastern Sea and Yan Anle of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The Han shu traces the Gongyang line from Hu Muzi of Qi through Ying Gong, Meng Qing, Sui Meng, to Yan Pengzu and Yan Anle.

sentences.zh: 彭祖為《春秋》嚴氏學，安樂為《春秋》顏氏學，又瑕丘江公傳《穀梁春秋》，三家皆立博士。

translations.literal: Pengzu constituted the Spring and Autumn learning of the Yan house in the strict-graph tradition, Anle constituted the Spring and Autumn learning of the Yan house in the facial-graph tradition; further Jiang Gong of Xiaqiu transmitted the Guliang Spring and Autumn; all three houses had Erudites established.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Pengzu founded the Gongyang line later distinguished as the strict-graph Yan school, Yan Anle the Gongyang line distinguished as the facial-graph Yan school; Jiang Gong of Xiaqiu taught the Guliang commentary—all three received doctoral chairs.

sentences.zh: 梁太傅賈誼為《春秋左氏傳訓詁》，授趙人貫公。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor to Liang Jia Yi composed Glosses on the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn and handed them on to Guan Gong of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Jia Yi of Liang wrote a gloss on the Zuo commentary and passed it to Guan Gong of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 丁恭字子然，山陽東緡人也。

translations.literal: Ding Gong, courtesy name Ziran, was a man of Dongmin in Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Gong, Ziran, came from Dongmin in Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 習《公羊嚴氏春秋》。

translations.literal: He studied the Yan Pengzu Gongyang Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He trained in Yan Pengzu's Gongyang commentary.

sentences.zh: 恭學義精明，教授常數百人，州郡請召不應。

translations.literal: Gong's learning in meaning was lucid and penetrating; in teaching he constantly had several hundred persons; provinces and commanderies invited and summoned him but he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: His exegesis was razor-sharp; hundreds sat at his feet, yet he ignored every provincial summons.

sentences.zh: 建武初，為諫議大夫、博士，封關內侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he became Grandee Remonstrant and Consultant and Erudite, and was enfeoffed as marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangwu's reign he was grandee remonstrant, Erudite, and marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷少府。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In 35 CE he became privy treasurer.

sentences.zh: 諸生自遠方至者，著錄數千人，當世稱為大儒。

translations.literal: Students who came from distant places, recorded on the rolls, were several thousand persons; his age styled him a great Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands enrolled from afar; contemporaries hailed him as a great master.

sentences.zh: 太常樓望、侍中承宮、長水校尉樊儵等皆受業於恭。

translations.literal: Grand Chamberlain Lou Wang, Palace Attendant Cheng Gong, Colonel of the Chang Waters Fan Shu, and others all received instruction under Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Wang, Cheng Gong, Fan Shu, and others had all been his pupils.

sentences.zh: 二十年，拜侍中祭酒、騎都尉，與侍中劉昆俱在光武左右，每事諮訪焉。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Libationer among Palace Attendants and Chief Commandant of Cavalry, together with Palace Attendant Liu Kun both at Guangwu's left and right; on each matter they were consulted.
translations.idiomatic: In 44 CE he became chief academician among palace attendants and chief commandant of cavalry, serving beside Liu Kun as Guangwu's constant advisers.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 澤果敢直言，數有據爭。

translations.literal: Ze was bold and outspoken, and repeatedly had reasoned disputes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ze spoke bluntly and often argued his case in debate.

sentences.zh: 後北地太守廖信坐貪穢下獄，沒入財產，顯宗以信臧物班諸廉吏，唯澤及光祿勳孫堪、大司農常衝特蒙賜焉。

translations.literal: Later the Administrator of Beidi, Liao Xin, sat in guilt for greed and filth and was cast into prison; his property was confiscated; Emperor Xianzong distributed Xin's embezzled goods among incorrupt officials, but only Ze together with Superintendent of the Household Sun Kan and Grand Minister of Agriculture Chang Chong specially received the grant.
translations.idiomatic: When corrupt governor Liao Xin of Beidi was stripped of his fortune, Emperor Ming gave the loot to honest officials; Zhou Ze, Sun Kan, and Chang Chong alone received shares.

sentences.zh: 是時京師翕然，在位者咸自勉勵。

translations.literal: At that time in the capital there was unanimity; those in office all encouraged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The capital buzzed with the story, and every official took it as a spur to integrity.

sentences.zh: 堪字子稺，河南緱氏人也。

translations.literal: Kan, courtesy name Zhi, was a man of Gou shi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kan, Zhi, came from Gou shi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 明經學，有志操，清白貞正，愛士大夫，然一毫未嘗取於人，以節介氣勇自行。

translations.literal: He was clear in classical learning, had aims and integrity, was pure, white, chaste, and upright, loved gentlemen, yet not a hair's worth did he ever take from others; by integrity and mettle he conducted himself.
translations.idiomatic: A classical scholar of spotless honor, he loved the company of gentlemen and never accepted a gift, living by sheer principle and courage.

sentences.zh: 王莽末，兵革並起，宗族老弱在營保間，堪常力戰陷敵，無所迴避，數被創刃，宗族賴之，郡中咸服其義勇。

translations.literal: At the end of Wang Mang, weapons and armor rose together; the clan's old and weak were between stockades; Kan constantly fought hard and penetrated the enemy, nowhere turning aside, was wounded by blades many times, and the clan relied on him; in the commandery all submitted to his righteousness and courage.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang fell and war engulfed the land, Sun Kan fought through sieges to shield his kin, took wound after wound, and won the county's admiration for valor.

sentences.zh: 建武中，仕郡縣。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu period he served in county office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangwu he held county posts.

sentences.zh: 公正廉潔，奉祿不及妻子，皆以供賓客。

translations.literal: He was fair, upright, and clean; his salary did not reach wife and children but was all used to supply guests.
translations.idiomatic: He was just and frugal: his stipend went to guests, not to his household.

sentences.zh: 及為長吏，所在有跡，為吏人所敬仰。

translations.literal: When he became a senior official, wherever he was there were traces; clerks and common people revered him.
translations.idiomatic: As a senior magistrate he left a mark everywhere and won the people's respect.

sentences.zh: 喜分明去就。

translations.literal: He delighted in clear separation of going and staying.
translations.idiomatic: He cared sharply about when to serve and when to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 嘗為縣令，謁府，趨步遲緩，門亭長譴堪禦吏，堪便解印綬去，不之官。

translations.literal: Once when he was magistrate he went to pay respects at the commandery office; his hurried step was slow; the gate pavilion chief rebuked Kan's chariot driver; Kan then unsealed his seals and ribbons and departed, not going to office.
translations.idiomatic: Once, visiting the commandery, he walked too slowly for the gate captain, who abused his driver; Sun Kan resigned on the spot and never took the post.

sentences.zh: 後復仕為左馮翊，坐遇下促急，司隸校尉舉奏免官。

translations.literal: Later he again took office as Governor of Left Fengyi; he sat in guilt for treating subordinates hastily and harshly; the Metropolitan Commandant memorialized impeachment and dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Left Fengyi he was impeached for driving his staff too hard and lost the post.

sentences.zh: 數月，徵為侍御史，再遷尚書令。

translations.literal: Within several months he was summoned as Palace Attendant Censor and after two promotions became Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he was recalled as palace attendant censor, then rose twice to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永平十一年，拜光祿勳。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongping he was appointed Superintendent of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: In 68 CE he became superintendent of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 堪清廉，果於從政，數有直言，多見納用。

translations.literal: Kan was pure and clean, decisive in governance, repeatedly had straight words, and much was adopted from his views.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kan governed cleanly and spoke plainly; the throne often took his advice.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以病乞身，為侍中騎都尉，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, on account of illness begging his person, he became Palace Attendant and Chief Commandant of Cavalry, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 75 CE he retired ill to a combined post as palace attendant and chief commandant of cavalry, and died there.

sentences.zh: 堪行類於澤，故京師號曰「二稺」。

translations.literal: Kan's conduct was of a kind with Ze's; therefore the capital styled them "the two Zhi."
translations.idiomatic: Because Sun Kan resembled Zhou Ze in conduct, Luoyang called them the two Zhi.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以澤行司徒事，如真。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Ze was ordered to act in the Minister of Education's affairs as if substantive.
translations.idiomatic: In 69 CE Zhou Ze was put in charge of the minister of education's duties as acting minister.

sentences.zh: 澤性簡，忽威儀，頗失宰相之望。

translations.literal: Ze's nature was plain; he neglected ritual bearing and rather lost the expectation due a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ze was blunt and careless of ceremony, which disappointed those who expected a grand minister's dignity.

sentences.zh: 數月，復為太常。

translations.literal: Within several months he again became Grand Chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was back as grand chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 清潔循行，盡敬宗廟。

translations.literal: Pure and clean in conduct, he exhaustively revered the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the ancestral cult with scrupulous purity.

sentences.zh: 常臥疾齋宮，其妻哀澤老病，窺問所苦。

translations.literal: He constantly lay ill in the fasting palace; his wife pitied Ze's old age and illness and peeped in to ask what pained him.
translations.idiomatic: He often kept vigil ill in the fasting hall; his wife, pitying his age, looked in to ask how he felt.

sentences.zh: 澤大怒，以妻干犯齋禁，遂收送詔獄謝罪。

translations.literal: Ze was greatly angry, because his wife had violated the fasting prohibition, thereupon seized her and sent her to the imperial prison to apologize for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Furious that she had broken the fast-day rule, he had her jailed to expiate the offense.

sentences.zh: 當世疑其脆激。

translations.literal: The age doubted him brittle and extreme.
translations.idiomatic: People thought him harsh and excessive.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「生世不諧，作太常妻，一歲三百六十日，三百五十九日齋。

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying of him: "Born into an unharmonious world, be Grand Chamberlain's wife—three hundred sixty days in a year, three hundred fifty-nine days fasting."
translations.idiomatic: A rhyme ran: marry the grand chamberlain and you fast three hundred fifty-nine days a year.

sentences.zh: 」十八年，拜侍中騎都尉。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Palace Attendant and Chief Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In 75 CE he was named palace attendant and chief commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後數為三老五更。

translations.literal: Later he repeatedly served as one of the Three Elders and Five Renewed.
translations.idiomatic: He later served several terms as elder of state at the great suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 建初中致仕，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the Jianchu period he retired from office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhang he retired and died at home.

sentences.zh: 鍾興字次文，汝南汝陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhong Xing, courtesy name Ciwen, was a man of Ruyang in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Xing, Ciwen, was from Ruyang in Runan.

sentences.zh: 少從少府丁恭受《嚴氏春秋》。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Privy Treasurer Ding Gong in receiving the Yan house Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Yan Pengzu's Gongyang commentary under Privy Treasurer Ding Gong.

sentences.zh: 恭薦興學行高明，光武召見，問以經義，應對甚明。

translations.literal: Gong recommended Xing's learning and conduct as lofty and clear; Guangwu summoned him to audience and asked him on classical meaning; his replies were very lucid.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Gong praised his learning; Guangwu quizzed him on the classics and liked his answers.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，拜郎中，稍遷左中郎將。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of him, appointed him Gentleman of the Palace, and gradually promoted him to Left Leader of Court Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named him a gentleman, then moved him up to left leader of court gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 詔令定《春秋》章句，去其復重，以授皇太子。

translations.literal: By edict he was ordered to fix the Spring and Autumn chapter-and-verse glosses, remove their duplications, and thereby hand them on to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to prune the Gongyang gloss for the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 又使宗室諸侯從興受章句。

translations.literal: Further he caused imperial-clan princes to follow Xing in receiving the chapter-and-verse glosses.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes were told to study the same gloss with him.

sentences.zh: 封關內侯。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 興自以無功，不敢受爵。

translations.literal: Xing himself considered that he had no merit and did not dare accept the noble.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Xing thought himself undeserving and tried to refuse the title.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「生教訓太子及諸王侯，非大功邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Sir, in teaching and training the heir apparent and the various kings and marquises—is it not a great merit?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You tutored the heir and the princes—is that not great service?"

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「臣師於恭。

translations.literal: Xing said: "Your servant took his teacher from Gong."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Xing replied, "My teacher was Ding Gong."

sentences.zh: 」於是復封恭，而興遂固辭不受爵，卒於官。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ding Gong was again enfeoffed, while Xing firmly declined and would not accept the noble; he ended by dying in office.
translations.idiomatic: The court renewed Ding Gong's title, but Zhong Xing still refused the marquisate and died in harness.

sentences.zh: 甄宇字長文，北海安丘人也。

translations.literal: Zhen Yu, courtesy name Changwen, was a man of Anqiu in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Yu, Changwen, came from Anqiu in Beihai.

sentences.zh: 清淨少欲。

translations.literal: He was pure, quiet, and had few desires.
translations.idiomatic: He lived simply and asked little of the world.

sentences.zh: 習《嚴氏春秋》，教授常數百人。

translations.literal: He studied the Yan Pengzu Spring and Autumn and in teaching constantly had several hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: He taught Yan Pengzu's Gongyang commentary to hundreds at a time.

sentences.zh: 建武中，為州從事，徵拜博士，稍遷太子少傅，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu period he became provincial staff, was summoned and appointed Erudite, was gradually promoted to Junior Tutor to the heir apparent, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangwu he rose from provincial aide to Erudite and junior tutor of the crown prince, dying in post.

sentences.zh: 傳業子普，普傳子承。

translations.literal: He transmitted the enterprise to his son Pu, and Pu transmitted it to his son Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen Pu inherited the school, Pu's son Zhen Cheng after him.

sentences.zh: 承尤篤學，未嘗視家事，講授常數百人。

translations.literal: Cheng was especially devoted to learning; he never looked to household affairs; in lecturing he constantly had several hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Cheng was still more single-minded, ignored domestic cares, and taught hundreds.

sentences.zh: 諸儒以承三世傳業，莫不歸服之。

translations.literal: The various Confucians, because Cheng for three generations transmitted the enterprise, none failed to submit and admire him.
translations.idiomatic: Classicists deferred to him for three generations of uninterrupted transmission.

sentences.zh: 建初中，舉孝廉，卒於梁相。

translations.literal: In the early Jianchu period he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and died as chancellor of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated Filial and Incorrupt in the Jianchu era, he died as chancellor of the Liang kingdom.

sentences.zh: 子孫傳學不絕。

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons transmitted learning without break.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants kept the school alive for generations.

sentences.zh: 樓望字次子，陳留雍丘人也。

translations.literal: Lou Wang, courtesy name Cizi, was a man of Yongqiu in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Wang, Cizi, was from Yongqiu in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 少習《嚴氏春秋》。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Yan Pengzu Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He trained in Yan Pengzu's Gongyang line.

sentences.zh: 操節清白，有稱鄉閭。

translations.literal: He held his integrity pure and white and had a good name in village and hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: His probity won praise in his home district.

sentences.zh: 建武中，趙節王栩聞其高名，遣使齎玉帛請以為師，望不受。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu period Prince Jie of Zhao, Xu, hearing his lofty name, dispatched an envoy bearing jade and silk to invite him to be teacher; Wang did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xu of Zhao sent jade and silk to retain him as tutor; Lou Wang refused.

sentences.zh: 後仕郡功曹。

translations.literal: Later he served the commandery as merit assessor.
translations.idiomatic: He later became commandery merit assessor.

sentences.zh: 永平初，為侍中、越騎校尉，入講省內。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongping he became Palace Attendant and Colonel of the Agile Cavalry and entered to lecture within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongping he was palace attendant and colonel of the agile cavalry, lecturing inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷大司農。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In 73 CE he became grand minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 十八年，代周澤為太常。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he replaced Zhou Ze as Grand Chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: In 75 CE he succeeded Zhou Ze as grand chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 建初五年，坐事左轉太中大夫，後為左中郎將。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jianchu, on account of an affair he was shifted left to Grand Counsellor of the Palace, later becoming Left Leader of Court Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: In 80 CE a demotion made him grand counsellor of the palace, then left leader of court gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 教授不倦，世稱儒宗，諸生著錄九千餘人。

translations.literal: He taught tirelessly; the age styled him patriarch among Confucians; students recorded on the rolls were more than nine thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: He never tired of teaching; contemporaries called him dean of the Ru; more than nine thousand students enrolled.

sentences.zh: 年八十，永元十二年，卒於官，門生會葬者數千人，儒家以為榮。

translations.literal: At age eighty, in the twelfth year of Yongyuan, he died in office; disciples who gathered for the funeral were several thousand persons, and Confucians deemed it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in 100 CE at eighty; thousands of students attended his funeral—a classicist's dream.

sentences.zh: 程曾字秀升，豫章南昌人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Zeng, courtesy name Xiusheng, was a man of Nanchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zeng, Xiusheng, was from Nanchang in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 受業長安，習《嚴氏春秋》，積十餘年，還家講授。

translations.literal: He received instruction in Chang'an, studied the Yan Pengzu Spring and Autumn, accumulated more than ten years, returned home, and lectured.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Yan's Gongyang in Chang'an for over a decade, then went home to teach.

sentences.zh: 會稽顧奉等數百人常居門下。

translations.literal: Several hundred persons such as Gu Feng of Kuaiji constantly dwelt at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds from Kuaiji, led by Gu Feng, boarded with him year round.

sentences.zh: 著書百餘篇，皆《五經》通難，又作《孟子章句》。

translations.literal: He authored more than a hundred chapters, all penetrating difficulties in the Five Classics, and also composed Chapter-and-Verse Glosses on Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote over a hundred essays on knotty points in the Five Classics and a gloss on Mencius.

sentences.zh: 建初三年，舉孝廉，遷海西令，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianchu he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, was promoted to magistrate of Haixi, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 78 CE a Filial-and-Incorrupt nomination took him to magistrate of Haixi, where he died.

sentences.zh: 張玄字君夏，河內河陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xuan, courtesy name Junxia, was a man of Heyang in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuan, Junxia, came from Heyang in Henei.

sentences.zh: 少習《顏氏春秋》，兼通數家法。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Yan Anle Spring and Autumn and was broadly conversant with several houses' methods.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered Yan Anle's Gongyang and several rival glosses.

sentences.zh: 建武初，舉明經，補弘農文學，遷陳倉縣丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he was recommended as Understanding the Classics, was supplemented as erudite of letters to Hongnong, and was promoted to assistant magistrate of Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwu he took a classical nomination, became tutor in Hongnong, then assistant magistrate of Chencang.

sentences.zh: 清淨無欲，專心經書，方其講問，乃不食終日。

translations.literal: Pure and quiet without desires, he concentrated his mind on the classics and commentaries; when he was in the midst of lecturing and questioning, then he did not eat the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: Austere and bookish, he would forget meals when debating texts.

sentences.zh: 及有難者，輒為張數家之說，令擇從所安，諸儒皆伏其多通，著錄千餘人。

translations.literal: When there were difficult points, he always spread out several houses' explanations, ordering listeners to choose what they trusted; the various Confucians all submitted to his wide mastery; those recorded on the rolls were more than a thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: On hard questions he laid out rival schools and let students pick; peers marveled at his range, and a thousand enrolled.

sentences.zh: 玄初為縣丞，嘗以職事對府，不知官曹處，吏白門下責之。

translations.literal: When Xuan at first was assistant magistrate, he once on official business answered at the commandery office, did not know where the bureau was; clerks informed the gate chief, who rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: New as county assistant, he once could not find the right office at commandery headquarters and was scolded by the gate staff.

sentences.zh: 時，右扶風琅邪徐業，亦大儒也，聞玄諸生，試引見之，與語，大驚曰：「今日相遭，真解□矣！

translations.literal: At that time Xu Ye of Langye in Right Fufeng was also a great Confucian; hearing that Xuan was a student, he tried summoning him to audience, and conversing with him, cried in great surprise: "To meet you today is truly to resolve what was obscure!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ye of Fufeng, another great scholar, met Zhang Xuan as a student and exclaimed that the encounter lifted every obscurity from the texts.

sentences.zh: 」遂請上堂，難問極日。

translations.literal: Thereupon he invited him up to the hall and posed difficult questions the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: He brought him to the hall and debated until nightfall.

sentences.zh: 後玄去官，舉孝廉，除為郎。

translations.literal: Later Xuan left office, was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, and was appointed gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuan later resigned, took a Filial-and-Incorrupt nomination, and became a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 會《顏氏》博士缺，玄試策第一，拜為博士。

translations.literal: It happened that the Yan-house Erudite post was vacant; Xuan in the examination policy came first and was appointed Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan Gongyang chair fell vacant, he topped the policy exam and won it.

sentences.zh: 居數月，諸生上言玄廉說《嚴氏》、《冥氏》，不宜專為《顏氏》博士。

translations.literal: Within several months students submitted a memorial saying Xuan also lectured on the Yan strict tradition and the alternate Yan subdivision (text reads 冥氏), and ought not solely to be Yan-house Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Within months students protested that he taught other Gongyang lines as well and should not monopolize the Yan chair.

sentences.zh: 光武且令還署，未及遷而卒。

translations.literal: Guangwu for the moment ordered him to return to his office, and before a promotion came he died.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu sent him back to his old post; he died before another promotion.

sentences.zh: 李育字元春，扶風漆人也。

translations.literal: Li Yu, courtesy name Yuanchun, was a man of Qi in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, Yuanchun, was from Qi in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 少習《公羊春秋》。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Gongyang Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He trained in the Gongyang commentary.

sentences.zh: 沉思專精，博覽書傳，知名太學，深為同郡班固所重。

translations.literal: He pondered deeply and specialized; he broadly read documents and transmissions, was known at the Imperial Academy, and was deeply esteemed by Ban Gu of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: A deep reader famed at the Imperial Academy, he won Ban Gu's respect.

sentences.zh: 固奏記薦育於驃騎將軍東平王蒼，由是京師貴戚爭往交之。

translations.literal: Gu submitted a memorial recommending Yu to General of Agile Cavalry, the king of Dongping, Cang; whereby noble and powerful in the capital vied to go associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu recommended him to Prince Liu Cang of Dongping, and Luoyang grandees crowded his door.

sentences.zh: 州郡請召，育到，輒辭病去。

translations.literal: When provinces and commanderies invited and summoned him, Yu would arrive, then always plead illness and depart.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever summoned, he would appear, plead sickness, and leave.

sentences.zh: 常避地教授，門徒數百。

translations.literal: He constantly fled the locale and taught; disciples were several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He taught in hiding to a few hundred pupils.

sentences.zh: 頗涉獵古學。

translations.literal: He broadly skimmed ancient learning.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in older scholarship.

sentences.zh: 嘗讀《左氏傳》，雖樂文采，然謂不得聖人深意，以為前世陳元、範升之徒更相非折，而多引圖讖，不據理體，於是作《難左氏義》四十一事。

translations.literal: Once he read the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn; although he delighted in its literary color, yet he said it did not obtain the sages' deep meaning; he thought that in former generations Chen Yuan, Fan Sheng, and their kind mutually criticized and refuted one another yet for the most part cited chart-prophecies and did not rely on rational pattern; thereupon he composed forty-one items of "Objections to the Meaning of the Zuo Tradition."
translations.idiomatic: He admired the Zuo commentary's prose yet doubted it captured the sages; he faulted Chen Yuan and Fan Sheng for dueling with apocrypha instead of reason, and wrote forty-one objections.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書令。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose twice to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及馬氏廢，育坐為所舉免歸。

translations.literal: When the Ma clan was cast down, Yu sat in guilt because those he had recommended was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ma faction fell, he was sent home for having recommended their men.

sentences.zh: 歲餘复徵，再遷侍中，卒於官。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was again summoned, was twice promoted to Palace Attendant, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was recalled, rose twice to palace attendant, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 何休字邵公，任城樊人也。

translations.literal: He Xiu, courtesy name Shaogong, was a man of Fan in Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu, Shaogong, was from Fan in Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 父豹，少府。

translations.literal: His father Bao was Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: His father He Bao had been privy treasurer.

sentences.zh: 休為人質樸訥口，而雅有心思，精研《六經》，世儒無及者。

translations.literal: Xiu as a man was plain and slow of tongue, yet he had elegant thought; he finely studied the Six Classics, and scholars of the age none reached him.
translations.idiomatic: Plain-spoken but brilliant, he plumbed the Six Classics deeper than any peer.

sentences.zh: 以列卿子詔拜郎中，非其好也，辭疾而去。

translations.literal: By edict, as a minister's son, he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace; it was not his liking, and he declined citing illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Named a gentleman as a minister's son, he disliked court life and resigned on health grounds.

sentences.zh: 不仕州郡。

translations.literal: He did not take office in province or commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He never served in provincial or commandery posts.

sentences.zh: 進退必以禮。

translations.literal: In advancing or withdrawing he always used ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Advance or retreat, he hewed to ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 太傅陳蕃辟之，與參政事。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Chen Fan summoned him to join in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Chen Fan brought him into government.

sentences.zh: 蕃敗，休坐廢錮，乃作《春秋公羊解詁》，覃思不窺門，十有七年。

translations.literal: When Fan was defeated, Xiu sat in dismissal and prohibition from office; thereupon he composed Glosses on the Gongyang Spring and Autumn, pondering so deeply that he did not peer out his gate for seventeen years.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Fan fell, He Xiu was banned from office and spent seventeen years indoors writing his Gongyang gloss.

sentences.zh: 又注訓《孝經》、《論語》、風角七分，皆經緯典謨，不與守文同說。

translations.literal: Further he annotated and glossed the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and wind-horn seven parts, all patterned on canonical models and not the same as pedants who cling to the letter.
translations.idiomatic: He also glossed the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and wind-omen lore, aiming at classical models rather than narrow literalism.

sentences.zh: 又以《春秋》駁漢事六百餘條，妙得《公羊》本意。

translations.literal: Further by the Spring and Autumn he refuted more than six hundred items in Han affairs, subtly obtaining the original intent of Gongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He used Gongyang to critique over six hundred Han precedents, capturing the school's core intent.

sentences.zh: 休善曆算，與其師博士羊弼，追述李育意以難二傳，作《公羊墨守》、《左氏膏肓》、《穀梁廢疾》。

translations.literal: Xiu was good at calendrical calculation; together with his teacher the Erudite Yang Bi he pursued and stated Li Yu's ideas to object to the two traditions, composing Gongyang Ink-Bound, Zuo Ailing, and Guliang Morbid.
translations.idiomatic: With his teacher Erudite Yang Bi he developed Li Yu's attacks on the Zuo and Guliang schools in three famous polemics.

sentences.zh: 黨禁解，又辟司徒。

translations.literal: When the faction prohibition was lifted, he was again summoned to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After the prohibition on partisans ended, the minister of education called him again.

sentences.zh: 群公表休道術深明，宜侍帷幄，單臣不悅之，乃拜議郎，屢陳忠言。

translations.literal: The high ministers memorialized that Xiu's Way and arts were profoundly clear and that he ought to attend within the curtain; petty ministers were displeased, and he was appointed Gentleman Consultant, repeatedly setting forth loyal words.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers wanted him at court; rivals blocked a high post, so he served as gentleman consultant and spoke frankly.

sentences.zh: 再遷諫議大夫，年五十四，光和五年卒。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Grandee Remonstrant and Consultant; at age fifty-four he died in the fifth year of Guanghe.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grandee remonstrant and died in 182 CE at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 服虔字子慎，初名重，又名祇，後改為虔，河南滎陽人也。

translations.literal: Fu Qian, courtesy name Zishen—at first his name was Chong, also named Zhi, later changed to Qian—was a man of Xingyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian, Zishen, born Chong, also called Zhi, later Qian, was from Xingyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 少以清苦建志，入太學受業。

translations.literal: In youth by pure austerity he set his aims and entered the Imperial Academy to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Poor but determined, he enrolled at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 有雅才，善著文論，作《春秋左氏傳解》，行之至今。

translations.literal: He had refined talent and was good at composing essays; he wrote Explication of the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn, which has been practiced to the present.
translations.idiomatic: His commentary on the Zuo tradition is still read.

sentences.zh: 又以《左傳》駁何休之所駁漢事六十條。

translations.literal: Further by the Zuo Tradition he refuted sixty items in what He Xiu had refuted in Han affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He answered He Xiu's sixty Han precedents with Zuo-based rebuttals.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，稍遷，中平末，拜九江太守。

translations.literal: He was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, was gradually promoted, and at the end of Zhongping was appointed Administrator of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and Incorrupt, he rose to governor of Jiujiang at the end of Zhongping.

sentences.zh: 免，遭亂行客，病卒。

translations.literal: Dismissed, he traveled as a guest amid disorder and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of office, he wandered as a refugee and died sick on the road.

sentences.zh: 所著賦、碑、誄、書記、《連珠》、《九憤》，凡十餘篇。

translations.literal: What he composed—fu, stele inscriptions, dirges, letters and records, Linked Pearls, and Nine Indignations—were in all more than ten pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His rhapsodies, steles, dirges, letters, linked pearls, and Nine Indignations fill more than ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 穎容字子嚴，陳國長平人也。

translations.literal: Ying Rong, courtesy name Ziyan, was a man of Changping in Chen state.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Rong, Ziyan, was from Changping in Chen.

sentences.zh: 博學多通，善《春秋左氏》，師傅太尉楊賜。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and conversant in many things, he was good at the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn and took Grand Commandant Yang Ci as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: A polymath, he mastered the Zuo commentary under Grand Commandant Yang Ci.

sentences.zh: 郡舉孝廉，州辟，公車徵，皆不就。

translations.literal: The commandery recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt; the province summoned; the imperial coach summoned; each time he did not take it up.
translations.idiomatic: He refused commandery, provincial, and imperial summonses.

sentences.zh: 初平中，避亂荊州，聚徒千餘人。

translations.literal: In the Chuping period he fled disorder to Jing province and gathered more than a thousand disciples.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chuping era he fled to Jingzhou with a thousand students.

sentences.zh: 劉表以為武陵太守，不肯起。

translations.literal: Liu Biao appointed him Administrator of Wuling; he was unwilling to rise to office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao offered him Wuling; he would not serve.

sentences.zh: 著《春秋左氏條例》五萬餘言，建安中卒。

translations.literal: He authored more than fifty thousand graphs of Regulations for the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn, and died in the Jian'an period.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote fifty thousand characters on Zuo procedure and died in the Jian'an years.

sentences.zh: 謝該字文儀，南陽章陵人也。

translations.literal: Xie Gai, courtesy name Wenyi, was a man of Zhangling in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Gai, Wenyi, came from Zhangling in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 善明《春秋左氏》，為世名儒，門徒數百千人。

translations.literal: He was good at clarifying the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn and was a famous Confucian of the age; disciples were several hundred to a thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: A celebrated Zuo scholar, he taught hundreds or thousands.

sentences.zh: 建安中，河東人樂詳條《左氏》疑滯數十事以問，該皆為通解之，名為《謝氏釋》，行於世。

translations.literal: In the Jian'an period Le Xiang of Hedong listed several dozen doubtful points in the Zuo Tradition to ask; Gai for them all gave penetrating explanations, naming it "Xie's Exegesis," which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Le Xiang of Hedong sent him dozens of Zuo puzzles in Jian'an; Xie Gai answered each in a work still called Xie's Exegesis.

sentences.zh: 仕為公車司馬令，以父母老，託病去官。

translations.literal: He served as overseer of the imperial coach, but because his parents were old he pleaded illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: As overseer of the imperial coach he quit to care for aging parents.

sentences.zh: 欲歸鄉里，會荊州道斷，不得去。
