translations.literal: He wished to return to his home village, but it happened that roads in Jing province were cut off and he could not go.
translations.idiomatic: He could not reach home because Jingzhou's roads were blocked by war.

sentences.zh: 少府孔融上書薦之曰：

translations.literal: Privy Treasurer Kong Rong submitted a memorial recommending him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong memorialized the throne on his behalf:

sentences.zh: 臣聞高祖創業，韓、彭之將征討暴亂，陸賈、叔孫通進說《詩》、《書》。

translations.literal: "Your servant has heard that when the High Ancestor founded the enterprise, the generals Han and Peng campaigned to strike down violence and disorder, while Lu Jia and Shu Sun Tong advanced discourses on the Odes and Documents."
translations.idiomatic: "When Gaozu built the dynasty, Han Xin and Peng Yue fought while Lu Jia and Shu Sun Tong preached the Odes and Documents."

sentences.zh: 光武中興，吳、耿佐命，範升、衛宏修述舊業，故能文武並用，成長久之計。

translations.literal: "At Guangwu's restoration, Wu and Geng aided the mandate, while Fan Sheng and Wei Hong repaired and continued the old learning; therefore civil and military were both employed and a long-term plan was achieved."
translations.idiomatic: "At Guangwu's revival Wu Han and Geng Yan won the field while Fan Sheng and Wei Hong restored the classics—civil and military together."

sentences.zh: 陛下聖德欽明，同符二祖，勞謙厄運，三年乃讙。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty's sagely virtue is reverent and bright, matching the tally of the two Founders; with labor and modesty you have endured ill fortune, and only after three years was there harmony."
translations.idiomatic: "Your sage virtue matches the two founders; through hardship you brought peace after three years of strife."

sentences.zh: 今尚父鷹揚，方叔翰飛，王師電鷙，群凶破殄，始有橐弓臥鼓之次，宜得名儒，典綜禮紀。

translations.literal: "Now the Grand Duke soars like a hawk, Fang Shu flies like a wing; the royal army strikes like lightning and the pack of villains is destroyed; we have reached the moment to bag bows and sleep on drums—it is fitting to obtain a famous Confucian to preside over ritual canons."
translations.idiomatic: "With generals triumphant and weapons ready to be stowed, the throne needs a great ritualist to codify ceremony."

sentences.zh: 竊見故公車司馬令謝該，體曾、史之淑性，兼商、偃之文學，博通群藝，周覽古今，物來有應，事至不惑，清白異行，敦悅道訓。

translations.literal: "Your servant has seen that the former overseer of the imperial coach Xie Gai embodies the fine nature of Zeng and Shi, combines the literary learning of Shang and Yan, is broadly conversant in the host of arts, has toured antiquity and the present, responds when things come, is not confused when affairs arrive, has conduct pure and white and unusual, and earnestly delights in the Way's instruction."
translations.idiomatic: "Xie Gai unites the virtues of Zeng and Shi, the learning of Shang and Yan, encyclopedic mastery, and unshakable judgment—pure, devoted, rare."

sentences.zh: 求之遠近，少有疇匹。

translations.literal: "Sought near and far, there are few who match him."
translations.idiomatic: "Few scholars anywhere rival him."

sentences.zh: 若乃巨骨出吳，隼集陳庭，黃能入寢，亥有二首，非夫洽聞者，莫識其端也。

translations.literal: "As for giant bones emerging in Wu, falcons gathering in Chen's courtyard, yellow bears entering the chamber, and the two heads on the day hai—unless one is broadly learned, none recognize the portents' beginnings."
translations.idiomatic: "Giant bones, omens in Chen, bears in the chamber, calendrical puzzles—only a learned man can read such signs."

sentences.zh: 雋不疑定北闕之前，夏侯勝辯常陰之驗，然後朝士益重儒術。

translations.literal: "Jun Buyi settled the affair before the northern gate tower; Xiahou Sheng debated the verification at Changyin—only afterward did court gentlemen all the more esteem Confucian arts."
translations.idiomatic: "Jun Buyi and Xiahou Sheng proved how classics settle crises—then the court prized the Ru."

sentences.zh: 今該實卓然比跡前列，間以父母老疾，棄官欲歸，道路險塞，無自由致。

translations.literal: "Now Gai truly stands shoulder to shoulder with those listed before; meanwhile, on account of his parents' old age and illness, he cast aside office wishing to return, but roads are perilous and blocked, and he has no means freely to arrive."
translations.idiomatic: "Xie Gai matches those worthies yet cannot reach his parents because the roads are closed."

sentences.zh: 猥使良才抱朴而逃，逾越山河，沉淪荊楚，所謂往而不反者也。

translations.literal: "To let a fine talent embrace simplicity and flee, crossing mountains and rivers, sinking in Jing and Chu—this is what is called going and not returning."
translations.idiomatic: "To lose such a man to the south would be an irreparable waste."

sentences.zh: 後日當更饋樂以釣由餘，克像以求傅說，豈不煩哉？

translations.literal: "Later will you not have to set out feasts and music to hook You Yu, carve an image to seek Fu Yue—would it not be troublesome?"
translations.idiomatic: "Must you later hunt the empire for a Fu Yue when the man is already found?"

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為可推錄所在，召該令還。

translations.literal: "Your servant foolishly thinks one may push and record where he is located, summon Gai, and order him to return."
translations.idiomatic: "I beg you trace him, recall him, and restore him to office."

sentences.zh: 楚人止孫卿之去國，漢朝追匡衡於平原，尊儒貴學，惜失賢也。

translations.literal: "The men of Chu stopped Xun Qing from leaving the state; the Han court pursued Kuang Heng to Pingyuan—honoring Confucians and esteeming learning is cherishing the worthy not to lose them."
translations.idiomatic: "Chu kept Xunzi; Han recalled Kuang Heng—states prosper when they keep their scholars."

sentences.zh: 書奏，詔即徵還，拜議郎。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict immediately summoned him back and appointed him Gentleman Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: The edict recalled him at once as gentleman consultant.

sentences.zh: 以壽終。

translations.literal: He ended by a full lifespan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in old age.

sentences.zh: 建武中，鄭興、陳元傳《春秋左氏》學。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu period Zheng Xing and Chen Yuan transmitted the learning of the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangwu, Zheng Xing and Chen Yuan taught the Zuo commentary.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令韓歆上疏，欲為《左氏》立博士，範升與歆爭之未決，陳元上書訟《左氏》，遂以魏郡李封為《左氏》博士。

translations.literal: At that time Director of the Masters of Writing Han Xin submitted a memorial desiring to establish an Erudite for the Zuo Tradition; Fan Sheng disputed with Xin and it was not decided; Chen Yuan submitted a memorial suing for the Zuo Tradition; thereupon Li Feng of Wei commandery was made Erudite for the Zuo Tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Director Han Xin asked for a Zuo doctoral chair; Fan Sheng objected; Chen Yuan argued back until Li Feng of Wei was named the first Zuo Erudite.

sentences.zh: 後群儒蔽固者數廷爭之。

translations.literal: Later Confucians who were obstinately blocking repeatedly disputed it at court.
translations.idiomatic: Obstructionist classicists then fought the appointment again and again in open court.

sentences.zh: 及封卒，光武重違眾議，而因不復補。

translations.literal: When Li Feng died, Guangwu heavily went against the host of opinions and for that reason did not again fill the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Feng died, Guangwu let the Zuo doctoral chair stay vacant rather than fight the faculty again.

sentences.zh: 許慎字叔重，汝南召陵人也。

translations.literal: Xu Shen, courtesy name Shuzhong, was a man of Shaoling in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shen, Shuzhong, came from Shaoling in Runan.

sentences.zh: 性淳篤，少博學經籍，馬融常推敬之，時人為之語曰：「《五經》無雙許叔重。

translations.literal: By nature he was simple and earnest; in youth he broadly studied the classics and records; Ma Rong constantly pushed and revered him; people of the time made a saying of him: "None can match across the Five Classics—Xu Shuzhong."
translations.idiomatic: Earnest and widely read, he won Ma Rong's respect; contemporaries said, "No one matches Xu Shuzhong across the Five Classics."

sentences.zh: 」為郡功曹，舉孝廉，再遷除洨長。

translations.literal: He became merit assessor for the commandery, was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, and after two promotions was appointed magistrate of Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commandery merit assessor, took Filial and Incorrupt, and became magistrate of Jiao after two promotions.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 初，慎以《五經》傳說臧否不同，於是撰為《五經異義》，又作《說文解字》十四篇，皆傳於世。

translations.literal: At first, Shen, because the Five Classics' transmissions and explanations judged good and ill differently, thereupon compiled them into Divergent Meanings of the Five Classics, and also composed Explaining Graphs and Analyzing Characters in fourteen chapters; all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the Five Classics glosses contradictory, he wrote Divergent Meanings of the Five Classics and the fourteen-scroll Shuowen jiezi, both still extant.

sentences.zh: 蔡玄字叔陵，汝南南頓人也。

translations.literal: Cai Xuan, courtesy name Shuling, was a man of Nandun in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xuan, Shuling, was from Nandun in Runan.

sentences.zh: 學通《五經》，門徒堂千人，其著錄者萬六千人。

translations.literal: His learning penetrated the Five Classics; disciples in his hall were a thousand persons, and those recorded on the rolls were sixteen thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Five Classics; a thousand sat in his hall and sixteen thousand names appeared on his rolls.

sentences.zh: 徵辟並不就。

translations.literal: Summons and appointments together he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He turned down every summons.

sentences.zh: 順帝特詔徵拜議郎，講論《五經》異同，甚合帝意。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun specially by edict summoned him and appointed Gentleman Consultant; he lectured on sameness and difference in the Five Classics and greatly accorded with the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun named him gentleman consultant to debate the Five Classics and was well pleased.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，出為弘農太守，卒官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant, went out to become Administrator of Hongnong, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to palace attendant, governed Hongnong, and died in post.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自光武中年以後，干戈稍戢，專事經學，自是其風世篤焉。

translations.literal: The judgment says: From the middle years of Guangwu onward, weapons of war gradually were stowed away; they devoted themselves to classical learning, and from this time that wind grew ever more earnest in the world.
translations.idiomatic: After mid-Guangwu the swords were sheathed and the court turned to the classics until scholarship dominated public life.

sentences.zh: 其服儒衣，稱先王，遊庠序，聚橫塾者，蓋布之於邦域矣。

translations.literal: Those who wore Confucian robes, called on the former kings, wandered in schools, and gathered at private academies were spread through the commanderies and domains.
translations.idiomatic: Men in scholars' dress, invoking the ancient kings, filled the schools and private lecture halls of every province.

sentences.zh: 若乃經生所處，不遠萬里之路，精廬暫建，贏糧動有千百，其耆名高義開門受徒者，編牒不下萬人，皆專相傳祖，莫或訛雜。

translations.literal: As for where classicists dwelled, they did not shrink from roads ten thousand li; refined huts were briefly raised, and carrying grain they moved in hosts of hundreds or thousands; those who by venerable name and high righteousness opened gates and received disciples—registers of names were not less than ten thousand persons, all exclusively handing down their ancestors' teaching, none daring to mix or corrupt it.
translations.idiomatic: Classicists traveled endless roads to study; a master would pitch a hut and draw hundreds carrying their own rice; famous teachers enrolled ten thousand pupils each, transmitting a single lineage without adulteration.

sentences.zh: 至有分爭王庭，樹朋私裡，繁其章條，穿求崖穴，以合一家之說。

translations.literal: It reached the point of dividing in dispute at the royal court, planting factions in private lanes, multiplying their articles and clauses, boring for crannies and crevices, in order to fit one house's theory.
translations.idiomatic: They wrangled in the palace, built cliques in the lanes, spun ever finer rules, and tortured the text to vindicate one school.

sentences.zh: 故楊雄曰：「今之學者，非獨為之華藻，又從而繡其鞶帨。

translations.literal: Therefore Yang Xiong said: "Today's scholars not only weave flowery embroidery for them, they also embroider their leather sashes."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong wrote that modern scholars do not merely trim the embroidery—they stitch new patterns on the belt itself.

sentences.zh: 」夫書理無二，義歸有宗，而碩學之徒，莫之或徙，故通人鄙其固焉，又雄所謂「譊々之學，各習其師」也。

translations.literal: The pattern of writing admits no duality, meaning returns to a single source, yet the host of pedantic specialists will not budge from their positions; therefore comprehensive scholars despise their obstinacy—this is also what Xiong meant by "wrangling learning, each practicing his own teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Texts should converge on one truth, yet narrow specialists refuse to yield; broad scholars scorn their rigidity—the wrangling schools Yang Xiong mocked.

sentences.zh: 且觀成名高第，終能遠至者，蓋亦寡焉，而迂滯若是矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, observe those who win fame and high rank—those who in the end can reach far are probably few; and to be so pedantic and stuck is thus.
translations.idiomatic: Few who win degrees ever rise to greatness; most remain mired in pedantry.

sentences.zh: 然所談者仁義，所傳者聖法也。

translations.literal: Yet what they discuss is benevolence and rightness; what they transmit is the sages' law.
translations.idiomatic: Still, their theme was humanity and justice, their legacy the teaching of the sages.

sentences.zh: 故人識君臣父子之綱，家知違邪歸正之路。

translations.literal: Therefore men knew the bonds of lord and minister, father and son; households knew the road to leave evil and return to right.
translations.idiomatic: So people learned the duties of ruler and father, and every home heard the call from wrong to right.

sentences.zh: 自桓、靈之間，君道秕僻，朝綱日陵，國隙屢啟，自中智以下，靡不審其崩離；

translations.literal: Between Huan and Ling, the ruler's way was chaff-like and perverse; the court's net daily crumbled; openings for the state repeatedly appeared; from middling intelligence downward, none failed to see its collapse and separation;
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Huan and Ling government rotted, court discipline frayed, and even common minds foresaw the fall—

sentences.zh: 而權強之臣，息其窺盜之謀，豪俊之夫，屈於鄙生之議者，人誦先王言也，下畏逆順勢也。

translations.literal: yet powerful ministers laid to rest their schemes to spy and steal; bold heroes submitted to the opinions of rustic scholars—because men recited the words of the former kings and inferiors feared the trend of rebellion and submission.
translations.idiomatic: yet warlords checked their usurpations and bravos bowed to village teachers—because the classics were on every tongue and men feared the moral verdict of history.

sentences.zh: 至如張溫、皇甫嵩之徒，功定天下之半，聲馳四海之表，俯仰顧眄，則天業可移，猶鞠躬昏主之下，狼狽折札之命，散成兵，就繩約，而無悔心，暨乎剝橈自極，人神數盡，然後群英乘其運，世德終其祚。

translations.literal: As for men such as Zhang Wen and Huangfu Song, whose merit settled half the realm and whose fame galloped beyond the four seas—looking up and down, they could have shifted the heavenly mandate—yet still they bowed beneath benighted lords, scrambled at orders scratched on slips, scattered their completed armies, submitted to bonds and cords, and had no heart of regret, until peel and bark wore to the limit and men and spirits had exhausted their reckoning; only then did heroes of the age ride their opportunity and dynastic virtue ended its reign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen and Huangfu Song held half the empire and could have seized the throne, yet they knelt to weak emperors, obeyed scraps of orders, disbanded their hosts, and accepted fetters without regret until ruin ran its course—then new heroes rose and the Han mandate closed.

sentences.zh: 跡衰敝之所由致，而能多歷年所者，斯豈非學之效乎？

translations.literal: Tracing the path by which decay was brought about, yet able to endure so many years—is this not the effect of learning?
translations.idiomatic: That rotten government lasted so long—does that not show the power of learning?

sentences.zh: 故先師垂典文，褒勵學者之功，篤矣切矣。

translations.literal: Therefore former teachers handed down canonical writings, praising and spurring the merit of learners—how deep, how urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The old masters left texts that honored study—earnestly, urgently.

sentences.zh: 不循《春秋》，至乃比於殺逆，其將有意乎！

translations.literal: Not to follow the Spring and Autumn, to the point of being likened to killing and treason—perhaps that carries a pointed meaning!
translations.idiomatic: To ignore the Spring and Autumn is almost to invite the charge of regicide—perhaps the historian meant that sting.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：斯文未陵，亦各有承。

translations.literal: The encomium says: This culture not yet sunk—each line had its heir.
translations.idiomatic: Verdict: the tradition had not died; each school found heirs.

sentences.zh: 塗方流別，專門並興。

translations.literal: Roads branched and currents parted; specialist houses rose together.
translations.idiomatic: Paths diverged and specialist lines multiplied.

sentences.zh: 精疏殊會，通閡相徵。

translations.literal: Fine and rough met in different unions; penetration and blockage cross-examined one another.
translations.idiomatic: Subtle and crude readings clashed; insight and obstruction tested each other.

sentences.zh: 千載不作，淵原誰澄？

translations.literal: If a thousand years produce no sage, who will clarify the deep source?
translations.idiomatic: When no sage appears for ages, who purifies the fountainhead?
